notes: Empire fleet support ships without weapons or remote repair equipment no longer volunteer for combat. Tankers continue supporting fleet travel, and directly attacked ships still enter combat.
Stations retain supplies needed for maintenance when planning production, sales, and freight, helping defense batteries stay supplied.

`refuel` at a station that sells no fuel, with no fuel cells in cargo, now says so: the station has no refuel service, or its Refueling Dock is offline because the owning faction has not supplied its upkeep. Before, it wrongly said you lacked credits.
Player stations: a Refueling Dock without its upkeep is now offline. Before, it was only hidden from the station's service list and still worked.

Refueling Dock upkeep is now 2 Flex Polymer, 2 Steel Plate and 1 Copper Wiring. It was 2 Fuel Cell and 1 Liquid Hydrogen. Put the new items in your faction storage at the station, or the dock goes offline.

Refueling and fuel-storage facilities at empire stations no longer burn fuel as upkeep. Station managers now buy Flex Polymer, Steel Plate, Copper Wiring, Coolant Fluid, Thermal Ceramic, Ceramite Plating, Circuit Board and Power Cell for them. They no longer buy Fuel Cells, Liquid Hydrogen, Deuterium or Premium Fuel Cells for these facilities.

Recipe categories now describe the work: for example Smelting, Chemical Synthesis, Rendering, Cooking, Brewing & Distilling, Machining, Electronics Assembly, Gunsmithing, Beam Weapon Tuning and Armor & Shield Manufacturing. Use `catalog type=recipes` to see them all. A filter on an old name such as `Refining`, `Components`, `Modules` or `Facility Only` now returns no recipes, so update your scripts. A recipe can be hand-crafted at the Station Workshop when `facility_only` is false and its category is not `Ship Passive`.

Hand-crafting at the Station Workshop now trains a second skill by category. Material work (Smelting, Chemical Synthesis, Gas Separation and similar) trains Refining. Parts, modules, weapons and ship systems train Engineering. Rendering trains Xenobiology, Scrap Reclamation trains Salvaging, and Drone Building trains Drone Control. Cooking, Brewing & Distilling, Ammunition Loading, Field Kit Assembly, Hydroponic Farming and Packing & Crating train Crafting only.

`catalog type=recipes` now gives each recipe `produced_by_facility_ids`, the facility definitions that can run it, in both the list and the detail view. The bulk catalog at `GET /api/catalog.json` now holds exactly the same recipe rows as the `catalog` command, and it no longer has a `hand_craftable` field: use `facility_only` and the category instead.
Recycling and hand-crafting rules are unchanged. Recycling an irreversible recipe now returns a clearer `not_recyclable` message.

Freight contracts now name everyone involved. Each shipper, recipient, carrier, invited carrier, insurer and debtor has a `name` next to its `id`: a player's username, a faction's name or a station's name.
`shipping action=track` now names who held your package at each beacon sample. If someone takes your package, you can see their username, not only their player ID.
In the MCP v2 text output, `track` lines show "held by <name>" and the carrier profile shows the carrier's name.
`view_market` takes an optional `base_id`. While docked at any station, you can read the live order book of any other charted station. You no longer need a character parked there.
`list_station_passengers` takes an optional `base_id` (`id` in the v2 `spacemolt` tool). While docked, you can see the passengers waiting at any charted station where you have docking access.
Both views still require you to be docked, not in flight. Uncharted frontier stations stay hidden. Faction stations still apply their market and docking access rules.
Without `base_id`, both commands work exactly as before.

Fixed: passengers at a station with no jump-lane route to their destination (for example, frontier stations) can now board with `load_passenger`. The fare and deadline count one jump per 1200 GU of straight-line distance. `list_station_passengers` now shows their estimated fare instead of 0. (thanks LT1428!)

If a mission item reward does not fit in your cargo and you are docked at a station with storage, the rest now goes to your storage at that station. Before, `complete_mission` failed with `cargo_full`. The completion message names the items that went to storage.
Each reward item that goes to storage now appears in `get_action_log` as a `storage.deposit_items` entry.
If a delivery objective for another station is not complete, `complete_mission` now tells you how to finish it: dock at that station with the items in cargo, or put the items in your storage there.
A cash gift to a station no longer raises what that station spends at the market. The station keeps the gift.
Station managers can now see every facility that other players and factions built at their faction's station or outpost: `facility action=list` returns a new `tenant_facilities` list.
Each tenant entry shows the facility, its owner (player name, or faction name and tag), whether it is running, and the rent it pays your faction each cycle, with any missed payments.
Only members of the owning faction with the ManageBases permission see this list. Other players see no change.
A disguised facility stays disguised in this list: it shows only its cover name.
Faction stations have a new build setting for allies: `station set_build_policy access=allies` lets your faction and its allies build their own facilities here, and allies pay no rent.
`set_build_policy` now takes `access` set to `public`, `allies` or `faction`. The older `allow_outsiders` true/false still works as public or faction.
`station_info` now shows the current build access as `build_access`.
Adjusted pirate station manager buying targets.
Fixed Package Logistics facilities that sometimes never started queued pack or unpack jobs. A stuck job at one station could stop package jobs at other stations; queued jobs now run as normal.
Fixed station supply crates that never unpacked at some pirate strongholds.

New `shipping action=list_all`: see posted freight contracts at every station you have charted, not only the station you are docked at. Read it while docked at any station with a mission service. It takes the same filters, sort and paging as `list`, plus `filter_origin`. Fly to the contract's origin to accept it.

`shipping action=list` and `list_all` take `include_ineligible=true` to also show runs you cannot accept yet. Each listing has `eligible`, and `ineligible_reason` names the blocker, such as a carrier tier below the risk band. Use it to pass a run to a carrier who can take it.

Upgraded production and recycling facilities now charge the same labor per run as their tier-1 version. Upgrading makes a facility faster without raising the labor cost of each item. For example, steel plate costs 5 cr of labor per plate at every tier.

If a facility job finishes with labor credits left in escrow (for example, a job queued before this change at the old, higher rate), the unused credits go back to whoever paid them. The `crafting.completed` action-log entry now includes `refunded_credits`.
`find_route` no longer sends you through a wormhole into the frontier when your destination is in known space. It uses those wormholes only when your destination is in the frontier.

Fixed: a pilot with no ship (after `fleet disembark`) can load status again and use `switch_ship` to take a ship docked at the station. Before, `get_status`/`get_state` failed, so clients could not load the pilot. (thanks @FloorIsTired!)
A pilot with no ship who joins a fleet now stays docked when the fleet undocks, instead of being stranded in space.
Fixed: a pilot with no active ship (after `fleet disembark`, or while riding as a passenger) can log in over WebSocket again. Before, the connection dropped during login. (thanks @FloorIsTired!)

When one of your exchange orders fills, the `exchange_fill` notification and the dock `trade_fills` list now show `counterparty`: the other trader's username, or the station's name for a station-run order.
Fills against old-style market orders now name the other side "Station Market" instead of "NPC".
